title: Prayer Against Enemies
overview: Psalm 83 is a fervent prayer attributed to Asaph, pleading with God not to remain silent in the face of a confederacy of nations conspiring against Israel. The psalmist vividly describes the enemies’ intent to annihilate Israel’s identity and heritage, calling upon God to act decisively as He did in past deliverances. This chapter highlights the reality of spiritual and physical opposition to God's people and underscores the necessity of divine intervention. It serves as a powerful reminder of God’s sovereignty over nations and His role as Israel’s protector, encouraging believers to seek God’s justice and acknowledge His supreme authority.
structure:
**Verses 1-5: The Plea for Divine Intervention.** The psalmist urgently calls on God not to be silent or still, emphasizing the threat posed by enemies who conspire to destroy Israel’s national identity.

**Verses 6-8: Identification of the Enemy Coalition.** A detailed list of hostile nations and peoples is presented, illustrating the broad and united opposition against Israel.

**Verses 9-15: A Call for Judgment Based on Historical Deliverances.** The psalmist appeals to God to deal with these enemies as He did with Midianites and other foes, invoking vivid imagery of destruction and divine wrath.

**Verses 16-18: The Desired Outcome and Divine Exaltation.** The prayer concludes with a plea for the enemies’ shame and confusion so that they may seek God’s name, affirming God’s unique sovereignty as Jehovah, the Most High over all the earth.

keyVerses.text: They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals the enemies’ explicit intent to annihilate Israel’s national identity, highlighting the existential threat faced by God’s people and the seriousness of their plea for divine protection.

keyVerses.text: Do unto them as unto the Midianites; as to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the brook of Kison:
keyVerses.significance: The psalmist invokes historical examples of God’s deliverance, reminding God of His past faithfulness and power to defeat Israel’s enemies, thus reinforcing trust in divine intervention.

keyVerses.text: Fill their faces with shame; that they may seek thy name, O LORD.
keyVerses.significance: This verse expresses the desire that God’s judgment would lead the enemies to repentance and recognition of His sovereignty, emphasizing the ultimate goal of God’s justice—restoration through acknowledgment of Him.

keyVerses.text: That men may know that thou, whose name alone is JEHOVAH, art the most high over all the earth.
keyVerses.significance: The concluding verse affirms God’s unique and supreme authority over all nations, underscoring the theological foundation that God alone is sovereign and worthy of worship.

characters.name: God (Jehovah)
characters.description: The sovereign Lord and protector of Israel, who is petitioned to act decisively against the enemies. God’s power and justice are central to the psalm’s plea for deliverance and vindication.

characters.name: The Enemies of Israel
characters.description: A coalition of nations including Edom, Ishmaelites, Moabites, Hagarenes, Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, Philistines, Tyrians, and Assyrians, united in their intent to destroy Israel’s identity and heritage.

characters.name: Asaph
characters.description: The psalmist and leader of worship who composes this prayer, expressing deep concern for Israel’s survival and appealing to God’s justice and past acts of deliverance.

themes.description: The psalm emphasizes God’s role as Israel’s defender against hostile nations, reflecting the biblical theme of God as a refuge and shield for His people.
The call for God to judge the enemies as He did in past victories highlights the theme of divine justice and the certainty of God’s righteous retribution.
The psalm culminates in the affirmation of Jehovah’s supreme authority over all the earth, reinforcing the biblical doctrine of God’s universal kingship.
The entire psalm is a model of earnest prayer, demonstrating the believer’s dependence on God’s intervention in times of national crisis.

historicalContext: Psalm 83 likely reflects a period of intense geopolitical tension during the divided monarchy or post-exilic era when Israel faced threats from neighboring peoples. The listed enemies correspond to known ancient nations surrounding Israel, such as Edom, Moab, and the Philistines, who frequently opposed Israel’s existence. The coalition described may represent a historical confederacy intent on erasing Israel’s identity, reflecting the precarious position of the nation amid regional hostilities. Understanding the customs of covenant loyalty and divine kingship in the Ancient Near East helps illuminate the psalmist’s appeal to God as Israel’s protector and judge. The invocation of past deliverances recalls God’s historical acts of salvation, reinforcing hope amid present danger.

theologicalInterpretations.description: This perspective sees Psalm 83 as a prayer for God’s sovereign justice against enemies of His covenant people, emphasizing God’s faithfulness to protect His elect and uphold His promises.

Dispensationalists often interpret Psalm 83 prophetically, viewing the enemies as modern or future nations conspiring against Israel, with the psalm anticipating God’s ultimate intervention in end-times conflict.

Early church interpreters frequently understood this psalm typologically, seeing Israel’s enemies as symbolic of spiritual opposition to God’s people, and the prayer as a call for divine victory over evil forces.

crossReferences.connection: The battle against Amalek parallels the enemies mentioned in Psalm 83, illustrating God’s past deliverance of Israel from hostile nations.
The defeat of Sisera and Jabin, referenced in Psalm 83:9-11, recalls God’s historic victories through judges, demonstrating His power to save Israel.
This verse promises that no weapon formed against God’s people shall prosper, reinforcing the theme of divine protection found in Psalm 83.
Paul’s instruction to leave vengeance to God aligns with the psalmist’s appeal for divine judgment against enemies.
Jehoshaphat’s prayer and God’s deliverance from a coalition of enemies echo the themes of Psalm 83, emphasizing trust in God’s intervention.

application: Trust God to defend and protect His people when facing opposition or persecution.
Pray earnestly for God’s justice against those who oppose His truth and people.
Remember and meditate on God’s past faithfulness to strengthen faith in present trials.
Seek God’s name and sovereignty above all, acknowledging His supreme authority.
Respond to spiritual and physical threats with prayer rather than fear or retaliation.
Encourage unity among believers to stand firm against common adversaries.
conclusion: Psalm 83 stands as a timeless prayer for God’s intervention against those who seek to destroy His people. It powerfully combines lament, historical remembrance, and confident petition, reminding believers that God alone is sovereign and able to deliver. The psalm encourages steadfast faith in God’s justice and protection, urging His people to seek His name and trust His power. For contemporary believers, it reinforces the call to persistent prayer and reliance on God amid spiritual and physical opposition, affirming that God’s name and glory will ultimately prevail.
timeline: c. 10th to 6th century BC, during the period of Israel’s divided monarchy or early post-exilic era when Israel faced hostile neighboring nations.

outline.heading: The Plea for God’s Attention
outline.description: The psalmist urgently appeals to God not to remain silent as enemies plot to destroy Israel’s identity, highlighting the severity of the threat.

outline.heading: The Enemy Coalition Named
outline.description: A detailed list of hostile nations and peoples united against Israel is presented, emphasizing the widespread opposition.

outline.heading: Invocation of Past Divine Deliverances
outline.description: The psalmist calls on God to act as He did in historic victories over Israel’s enemies, using vivid imagery of destruction and divine power.

outline.heading: Prayer for Shame and Recognition of God’s Sovereignty
outline.description: The psalm concludes with a plea that enemies be put to shame so they might seek God’s name, affirming God’s unique and supreme authority over all the earth.
